maria: quick heads-up — running into a nasty runtime problem when apps include our Java SDK alongside their own Jackson 2.15 dependency. stacktrace shows a NoSuchMethodError in com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.introspect.Annotated

sam: can you paste the exact stacktrace and the dependency tree? usually shading solves these but want to see if it's a conflicting minor version

maria: here's the top part of the trace
```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.introspect.Annotated.getAllAnnotations()Lcom/fasterxml/jackson/annotation/JsonIgnoreProperties;
	at com.redwood.client.json.JacksonAdapter.serialize(JacksonAdapter.java:48)
	at com.redwood.client.http.OkHttpTransport.request(OkHttpTransport.java:127)
	... 45 more
```

also our SDK pom has `com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:2.12.3` shaded into the jar using shadow relocation. The host app has 2.15. Is it safe to rely on relocation for jackson?

kevin: relocation is fine in principle but only if you relocate all jackson packages we reference (core, databind, annotations, module-kotlin if applicable). Partial relocation leaves runtime bindings broken.

julie: plus okhttp interceptors can serialize/deserialize too — double check no one in the host app is using a custom module that expects the original jackson classes by identity

maria: good point. also noticed streaming endpoint behaves differently when the host app enables gzip interceptor: our response body parsing fails mid-stream with EOFException sometimes

sam: gzip could wrap chunked streams and cause read boundaries to change. For OkHttp streaming endpoints:
- don't buffer the entire response in an interceptor
- use response.body().source() directly and avoid `string()` on large streams

kevin: also check OkHttp client config. In some test apps we saw the SDK-created OkHttpClient has `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)` and connect/read timeouts short — that interacts badly with proxies and chunked streaming. Recommend exposing client config or builder.

maria: current code snippet we use to create client:
```
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .readTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60))
    .writeTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60))
    .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
    .build();
```
would you suggest changing defaults?

kevin: two suggestions:
1) default retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for streaming-heavy endpoints; let callers opt in
2) expose a `.newBuilder()` that copies our client so apps can tweak connection pools/timeouts

sam: for shading jackson, a checklist that worked for us:
- use Gradle Shadow/ Maven Shade and relocate `com.fasterxml.jackson` -> `com.redwood.shaded.jackson` (all modules)
- include `jackson-annotations`, `jackson-core`, `jackson-databind`, and any module packages used
- run `mvn dependency:tree` or `./gradlew dependencies` for the final artifact to verify no raw com.fasterxml.* remains

maria: how about making SDK tolerant if host app provides a newer Jackson on the classpath? e.g., try to detect and fall back to using host jackson if available?

julie: that is possible but complex — you'd need to avoid classloader conflicts and provide a clear precedence strategy. We could provide two artifacts: `client` (shaded) and `client-no-shade` (no jackson included) and document compatibility.

kevin: +1 for split artifacts. Many libs do that: `artifact` and `artifact-no-shade`/`artifact-runtime`. Simpler for users who already manage jackson themselves.

sam: also a quick note on gson vs jackson: our Kotlin models use jackson annotations; if a host app tries to register a Gson converter it won't automatically work. Recommend documenting serialization extension points and providing a small adapter interface.

maria: ok plan:

- add tests that run SDK inside a small app with jackson 2.15 on classpath to reproduce linkage error in CI
